causes: [PLEADED ON INFORMATION AND BELIEF] Penal Code § 290.46(j) — hire at the Tracy DC on or about August 2024, then an employment decision; inference from Home Depot screening practice, Plaintiff's contemporaneous registry listing, and the July 2024 First Advantage/UPS report showing this Plaintiff was commercially matched to the California registry that season; Home Depot's own report is not in hand

key_facts: On or about August 2024, Plaintiff was hired to work at The Home Depot distribution/fulfillment center at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377 (San Joaquin County). Home Depot thereafter made an employment decision concerning that hire. Plaintiff is a Penal Code § 290 registrant whose identifying information appeared on the California Megan's Law website at the time. No offer letter, time records, wage statements, vendor name, or adverse-action notice is in the portfolio. The load-bearing theory is information-and-belief use of § 290.46 disclosures for employment. Supporting inference, not proof of Home Depot's file: Home Depot is a national employer that ordinarily backgrounds distribution-center hires; Plaintiff was on the registry; and in July 2024 First Advantage matched this same Plaintiff to SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY on the UPS employment report later lodged in E.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-02847. That UPS report is not alleged to have been sent to Home Depot and First Advantage is not alleged to have been Home Depot's vendor. The legal defendant is Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., not the Tracy building. Proposed California agent (verify on SOS before service): CSC Lawyers Incorporating Service, 2710 Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 150N, Sacramento, CA 95833.
procedural_status: Verified complaint review draft generated for proposed September 8, 2026 execution; deliberately unsigned and unfiled. Pre-execution gates: (1) confirm hire/start date, title, shift, and pay; (2) confirm what the employment decision was and its date; (3) confirm any BGC vendor, portal, or written notices; (4) confirm wages earned/lost and replacement work; (5) verify the current California agent for Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.; (6) execute on or after September 8 only after those confirmations. No CRD charge. No demand. Filing court is San Joaquin Superior Court. Companion Judicial Council forms (CM-010, summons, fee waiver) are not yet generated.
damages: No wage rate or duration is in the record. Portfolio valuation is $0 until the hire and decision are documented. Contingent statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: High-risk I&B draft, not filing-ready. The file has no Home Depot offer, report, or notice. Lerma dismissed a Megan's Law count where the report showed ordinary court records and no registry hit — this complaint stands or falls on what Home Depot's report says. CCP § 340(a) one-year penalty characterization remains a defense argument on the civil-penalty piece. Tameny is omitted because a two-year clock from an August 2024 decision would have run before September 8, 2026. Naming the Tracy building instead of Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. would be a party defect; serving the warehouse instead of CSC would be a service defect.
